-4.00000,17.60000.desc: A decision on a living modified organism, filed by the country itself to the Biosafety Clearing-House. Article 20 of the Cartagena Protocol requires every party to file its release and market decisions there within fifteen days, and 173 parties are bound by it. The United States is not among them. Nowhere else holds national release decisions from this many countries in one place. A country with no records here has not necessarily approved nothing — it may not have filed, and from the outside those two look the same.

-117.15200,32.80150.name: Fertility Specialists Medical Group
-117.15200,32.80150.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Wendy B. Shelly, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-98.92476,19.27482.name: PROGEN MÃ©xico Guadalupe
-98.92476,19.27482.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: www.progenzac.com. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere. No street address resolved, so this point is the city or the country rather than the centre.

5.40221,43.28844.name: Aix-Marseille University (AMU) -The "Unité des Virus Emergents"
5.40221,43.28844.state: 27, Bd Jean Moulin, 13005 Marseille cedex 05, France
5.40221,43.28844.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by Faculté de Médecine de Marseille. It is categorised as a university laboratory, working on human health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-68.20390,44.38760.name: Jackson Laboratory — Bar Harbor
-68.20390,44.38760.desc: The Maine campus where the strain collection is maintained and distributed, one of a small number of places in the world holding a genetic archive of this size. A fire in 1989 destroyed part of the colony and strains were rebuilt from material other laboratories had received — the distribution network turned out to be the backup.

-79.93110,32.77650.name: Charles River — horseshoe crab and LAL supply
-79.93110,32.77650.desc: Horseshoe crab blood is used to test injectable drugs and devices for bacterial contamination, and the animals are bled and returned to the sea with a proportion dying. A recombinant substitute exists, works, and is in the US pharmacopoeia; adoption has been slow because the old test is what everyone is used to.

-91.53000,41.66100.name: Genetic ID / Eurofins — public GMO testing
-91.53000,41.66100.desc: Accepts samples from anyone, not only from commercial clients. A PCR test on seed, grain or leaf tissue costs on the order of a hundred to a few hundred dollars and returns whether engineered material is present and often which event it is. That result is the difference between saying a neighbour’s crop reached your field and being able to show it. Ask for the event identification rather than a presence-or-absence screen: knowing WHICH trait is what ties the material to a particular seed and a particular grower.
